note: Reviewed corrections to typographical errors in the consolidated act's own text. Each one is a difference between the two places the act states the same statement, where one of them is plainly a typing error and the other is the sentence the regulation intends. Applied per code and per language, and only when the stored text still matches `wrong` exactly - if the source is corrected upstream, the erratum stops applying rather than overwriting the new text.

corrections.wrong: Thaw frosted parts with lukewarm water. Do no rub affected area.
corrections.corrected: Thaw frosted parts with lukewarm water. Do not rub affected area.
corrections.reason: "Do no rub" is not a sentence. The same act prints "Do not rub" where it selects the statement.
corrections.evidence: Annex IV Part 1, Table 6.3 (Precautionary statements - Response), row P336, block ▼B: "Thaw frosted parts with lukewarm water. Do not rub affected area." Part 2's English column of the same consolidation drops the "t".
